name: input-leap
description: 'Auto Config' auto-downloads a Bonjour MSI over plaintext HTTP and runs msiexec /i /passive with zero verification — on-path RCE. [Opus-verified: CONFIRMED-D]
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: input-leap’s Auto Config downloads Bonjour over HTTP and invokes msiexec without payload verification. This is a dependency installer channel, not a primary app updater.
limitations: Source review is limited to the retained commit and does not establish released-artifact or current-upstream behavior.

original_evidence.text: | input-leap | https://github.com/input-leap/input-leap (clone: repos/AL4/input-leap) | 34a34fb / 2025-11-28 | N (no self-updater for InputLeap itself) | N | **Y (side-channel: 3rd-party dependency installer)** | **http — PLAINTEXT, no TLS at all** | N | **none** | n/a | `src/gui/src/MainWindow.cpp:67` `bonjourBaseUrl = "http://binaries.symless.com/bonjour/"`; `:1289-1332` `downloadBonjour()` fetches `Bonjour.msi`/`Bonjour64.msi` over plain HTTP via `DataDownloader` (`src/gui/src/DataDownloader.cpp` uses bare `QNetworkAccessManager`, no cert/hash checks); `:1335-1372` `installBonjour()` writes the downloaded bytes straight to a temp file and launches `msiexec /i <file> /passive` with **zero hash or signature verification** of the downloaded MSI before execution. Triggered automatically when user enables "Auto Config" (`promptAutoConfig()` / `on_m_pCheckBoxAutoConfig_toggled`, same file ~1385-1430). |
